title: SJB MP Chaminda Wijesiri sentenced to 18 months in prison - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 28 (Daily Mirror) - Badulla District MP Chaminda Wijesiri has been sentenced to one-and-a-half years' imprisonment after being convicted by the Badulla High Court over a 2019 incident involving police officers.

The High Court found Wijesiri guilty of wrongful restraint, assault causing bodily harm, and criminal intimidation of police officers during an altercation near the Bandarawela roundabout.

The prosecution said the incident occurred in 2019 after a police jeep overtook the MP's vehicle, triggering an argument that escalated into the assault and intimidation of police officers.

title: SriLankan links to 17 Maldives destinations - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 28 (Daily Mirror) - SriLankan Airlines has expanded its regional network by signing a new interline agreement with Island Aviation Services, operating as Maldivian (Q2), enabling passengers to travel seamlessly to 17 domestic destinations across the Maldives under a single ticket.

The agreement allows passengers to book combined itineraries on SriLankan Airlines and Maldivian using a single electronic ticket for both inbound and outbound travel via Velana International Airport in Malé and Gan International Airport on Gan Island.

The partnership links SriLankan Airlines' international network with Maldivian's domestic services, offering easier access to remote and popular islands in the Maldives. The airline said the move is expected to benefit both leisure and business travellers by providing smoother transfers throughout the archipelago.

SriLankan Airlines currently operates three daily flights to Velana International Airport in Malé and two weekly flights to Gan International Airport, providing strong connectivity between Sri Lanka and the Maldives while offering onward connections through its international network.

The airline said the interline agreement would also create new opportunities for travel agents, tour operators, corporate travel planners and individual travellers by simplifying bookings and supporting passenger growth on the Malé and Gan routes.

"Our collaboration with Maldivian represents an important milestone in expanding our regional footprint and enhancing travel convenience for our customers. By integrating our global network with Maldivian's domestic connectivity, we are unlocking greater access across the Maldives while creating new opportunities for growth across key commercial segments," Head of Commercial Dimuthu Tennakoon said.

Maldives Manager Nayomi Tennakoon said the partnership provides passengers with seamless access from SriLankan Airlines' global network through Malé and Gan to numerous domestic destinations across the Maldives on a single itinerary.

SriLankan Airlines said the initiative reflects its continued commitment to improving connectivity, convenience and travel options across the region.

The national carrier serves 130 destinations in 63 countries, including codeshare services, and operates direct flights to 33 destinations with an all-Airbus fleet comprising A330-200/300 and A320/321 aircraft.

title: India recall Jadeja for Sri Lanka Tests - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
July.28 (Mirror Sports) - Shubman Gill will lead India in a two-Test series against Sri Lanka, with the opening match set to begin in Galle on August 15 as part of the ICC World Test Championship 2025-27.

The biggest talking point is the return of all-rounder Ravindra Jadeja, who is back in India's Test squad for the first time since January after recovering from a tennis elbow injury that kept him sidelined since May.

Sai Sudharsan and Jasprit Bumrah have also been named in the squad, although both remain subject to fitness.

KL Rahul has been appointed vice-captain, while Rishabh Pant, Yashasvi Jaiswal and Dhruv Jurel bolster the batting line-up. Kuldeep Yadav will partner Jadeja in the spin department, while Mohammed Siraj, Prasidh Krishna and Gurnoor Brar provide the pace options.

India head into the series looking to bounce back after recent Test series defeats to New Zealand, South Africa and Australia. However, they have won their last two Test series in Sri Lanka, claiming victories in 2015 and 2017.

The first Test will be played in Galle from August 15-19, with the second scheduled for Colombo from August 23-27.

title: Oil prices fall 1% as investors weigh pause in US strikes on Iran - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
EURONEXT - Oil prices fell 1% on Tuesday as market participants continued to weigh a pause in U.S. strikes on Iran, which has raised hope of a diplomatic solution to their conflict and the normalisation of Middle East energy flows.

Brent crude futures were down $0.54, or 0.6%, at $87.82 by 0046 GMT. U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude was at $81.95 a barrel, down $0.66, or 0.8%.

Both contracts fell 1% earlier in the session to their lowest level in more than a week.

U.S. President Donald Trump said on Monday the United States was having "good talks" with Iran and that there was a chance of a resolution. However, he said U.S. strikes would resume if negotiations failed while Iran issued similar comments about retaliation.

"For now, the relief that an off-ramp has been found has taken the heat out of prices and eased concerns around Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure. However, the situation remains highly fluid," IG analyst Tony Sycamore said in a client note.

Afrah al-Zouba, the foreign minister-designate of Yemen's internationally recognised Saudi-backed government, said Yemen-based Houthi fighters aimed to replicate Iran's control of shipping through the Strait of Hormuz at Bab el-Mandeb.

"Whether the Houthis have the military capacity to enforce a comprehensive blockade is questionable, especially given that the Saudis will attack them relentlessly. Still, there is no doubt that traffic has dropped off significantly in the Red Sea and the Strait of Hormuz," said Marex analyst Edward Meir.

"A key reason prices are not even higher than they are right now is the demand destruction that is taking place, especially in Asia," Meir said.

Barclays analysts said in a note on Monday "flows through the strait remain subdued". They said, in the week ended July 24, crude oil and refined product net exports through the strait averaged 2.9 million barrels a day compared with 5.9 million in the previous week.

Elsewhere, U.S. crude oil stockpiles likely fell last week alongside gasoline, while distillate stocks likely rose, a preliminary Reuters poll showed on Monday.

title: LPL 2026 Playoff Race Heats Up - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
July.28 (Mirror Sports) - The Lanka Premier League 2026 has entered its decisive phase, with six league matches remaining before the playoffs. Dambulla Sixers and Kandy Royals are also in the hunt, making every remaining fixture crucial in the battle for the top four.

Kandy Royals' Lahiru Udara leads the Orange Cap race with 222 runs, while teammate Nuwan Thushara tops the Purple Cap standings with 11 wickets. The top four teams will qualify for the playoffs, which begin on August 5 at the R. Premadasa International Cricket Stadium in Colombo. The LPL 2026 final is scheduled for August 8.
